beats.said: This is a hyaluronic acid filler and we're gonna use a cannula. I like using cannulas because they're blunt. Cannulas are a much more advanced delicate way of actually injecting fillers and you'll see that afterwards she'll look great and these fillers typically last anywhere from a year to a year and a half.

beats.said: a bit of anesthetic already in the filler. It's what we call lidocaine.

beats.said: inject the filler deep into the tissue. We basically go right underneath the muscle
beats.noun: the fan map: the read entry point and the cannula paths drawn on her face in the injection footage, head-tracked; the section card: deep, under the muscle

beats.said: her lower eyelid is fuller on the right versus here where it's kind of deeper.

beats.said: the issue that comes up in these situations is do we want to put another syringe in there? And I always take into account the fact that this is going to expand. We never want to have a patient who has this pillowy look under the eyelids because it doesn't just look right. In her situation, there's already a really beautiful improvement. Again, the key is to inject deep to avoid that bluish hue called the Tyndall effect.
